anomalies.observed: The anodes of the three status LEDs D2 (green), D23 (green) and D39 (yellow) all sit on /NET0086, and that net contains only those three anode pins. No other component or power rail is on it, so the LED anodes are not connected to +3V3. Their cathodes go through R27, R43 and R47 to the Ethernet nLED2/nLED3 and PI_nLED_Activity outputs.
anomalies.expected: These are active-low status LEDs. Their anodes must be tied to the 3.3 V rail (+3V3) so that a low drive from the CM4 or Ethernet PHY lights them. Other status LEDs in the design (e.g. D14, D16) are fed from +3V3 through a series resistor.
anomalies.impact: The three status LEDs cannot receive current from the 3.3 V rail, so the Ethernet activity/link indicators and the PI activity indicator stay dark. This is a visible functional fault, though not a board-level short.

anomalies.observed: R50 is valued "24k", but its library description and MPN describe a 24 Ω part: description "...±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor" and MPN "FRC0805J240TSD" (the '240' code denotes 24 Ω). The value field and the sourced part disagree by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: A 24 kΩ resistor across the PoE output pair (a 25 kΩ-class signature resistor). The part and value should agree, so a 24 kΩ part (e.g. code 243) should be sourced.

evidence.quote: (description " 125mW Thick Film Resistors 150V ±100ppm/℃ ±5% 24Ω 0805 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount ROHS")

anomalies.impact: If the 24 Ω part is fitted, the PoE/power-detection network is wrong. It would load the 50 V output with a heavy short-like resistance and cause the detection or bleed behaviour to fail.

anomalies.observed: CAN Interface A (J17) and CAN Interface B (J33) are wired to identical nets on every pin. Both connectors' CANH and CANL lines are shared with both isolated transceivers U44 and U48, so the two CAN buses are bridged together at the connectors.
anomalies.expected: Each M12 CAN interface should carry its own isolated bus (U44 to one connector, U48 to the other). The two buses must not share CANH/CANL nets.
anomalies.impact: The two CAN buses share one physical bus at the connectors. This defeats the isolation and independence of CAN0 and CAN1, and can cause bus contention, loss of motor-controller communication and e-stop/termination faults.

parsed.summary: The netlist shows three status LEDs whose anodes sit on an isolated net with no connection to +3V3, which would keep those indicators dark. The value of R50 (24k) also contradicts its 24 Ω part, and the two CAN connectors share all CANH/CANL nets. The first is the most likely fault; the others are lower confidence.
